Signals / Financial crime

Fraud, scams, sanctions, and control evidence

The financial-crime topic page turns public-source fraud, AML, sanctions, cryptoasset, and scam signals into ownership, prevention, detection, and escalation questions.

This week

Top 5 financial-crime signals

These items anchor the weekly read across fraud, AML, sanctions, cryptoasset controls, and customer harm.

  • OFSI issues its largest sanctions penalty since Russia's 2022 invasion, and its first for circumventionEnforcement / HM Treasury and OFSI / 2026-06-17
  • FCA finds firms have improved sanctions controls but gaps remain in screening and frozen-asset managementPrimary / FCA / 2026-05-28
  • Payment fraud falls by £73m as independent review confirms APP reimbursement policy is workingPrimary / Payment Systems Regulator / 2026-07-01
  • Operation Atlantic freezes $12m and identifies 20,000 victims of cryptocurrency approval-phishing fraudEnforcement / National Crime Agency / 2026-04-09
  • FCA finalises landmark cryptoasset regime rules, extending market-integrity and financial-crime expectations to crypto firmsPrimary / FCA / 2026-06-30

Why it made the weekly brief

The editorial judgement

Financial crime matters when external threat, customer harm, regulatory expectation, and the evidence that controls actually worked meet in the same operating question.

So what

Financial crime is a customer and control story

The best signal is not only loss. It is whether the firm can show prevention, detection, escalation, redress, and learning before harm repeats.

Who cares

MLRO, fraud, sanctions, payments, product, conduct, and board owners

The same signal can sit across AML, sanctions, scam reimbursement, cryptoasset exposure, and Consumer Duty.

Evidence needed

Risk assessment, typologies, alerts, decisions, and outcomes

Controls need to evidence why a scenario exists, when it fired, how it was dispositioned, and what customer or regulatory action followed.

Financial crime evidence checklist

What the reader should ask for

This checklist gives financial-crime owners practical prompts that can move straight into a review, committee pack, or assurance request.

  • RiskWhich typologies, channels, products, geographies, and customer segments changed this week?Assess
  • ControlsWhich prevention, screening, monitoring, and escalation controls map to those typologies?Map
  • AlertsCan the firm explain alert quality, suppression, overrides, backlogs, and false-positive trends?Monitor
  • HarmHow are scam losses, complaints, reimbursement, vulnerable customers, and repeated exposure tracked?Outcome
  • BoardWhat changed in the board view of financial-crime risk, appetite, resourcing, and remediation?Govern
